title: Who does it? én, te, ő

sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Each person has its own ending: *olvasok* (I), *olvasol* (you), *olvas* (he, she). So the verb already shows who does it, and you can leave out *én* and *te*. Say the pronouns when you set people against each other: *Én főzök, te olvasol, ő ír.*
After *ki* (“who”) the verb is the plain stem: *Ki olvas?* A bare *Olvas.* out of the blue leaves the listener asking who, so give a name or *ő* unless it is already clear.
